headline: SpaceX cashes in. Blue Origin stumbles. VCs circle.
deck: This week highlights major defense contracts and funding rounds, with a side of timing mishaps.

stories.head: SpaceX nets $4.16B for airborne tracking network
stories.body: The Space Force awarded SpaceX a $4.16 billion contract to develop a satellite network for tracking airborne threats, further solidifying its role in the defense sector. This contract follows a pattern where defense budgets seem to have no ceiling, especially when it comes to SpaceX. With this win, SpaceX continues to demonstrate that its value proposition extends beyond just launching rockets.
stories.soWhat: If SpaceX keeps landing these contracts, it might just become the military’s favorite child—watch out, Blue Origin.

stories.head: Blue Origin's timing fails spectacularly post-launch order
stories.body: Blue Origin received a national security launch task order just hours before a New Glenn explosion, a reminder that in aerospace, timing is everything—especially when it involves rocket launches. The company is still trying to recover from this setback, as it also grapples with the implications for future contracts. As they say, failure is not an option, but it seems Blue Origin is testing that theory.
stories.soWhat: If this keeps up, Blue Origin may need to rethink its marketing strategy—'We launch rockets, and sometimes they explode.'

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense hype
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding comes as the company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas that are increasingly prioritized by the DoD. Investors seem to be betting that cash will flow as fast as the threats in space.
stories.soWhat: In a world where cash often trumps innovation, True Anomaly's funding is a clear signal that defense dollars are the new gold.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's next contract could be bigger
watchlist.body: With the recent $4.16 billion deal, the market will be watching for further contracts as SpaceX continues to expand its defense portfolio.

watchlist.title: Blue Origin's recovery strategy
watchlist.body: Expect Blue Origin to outline a clear recovery strategy in the wake of the New Glenn explosion, as they need to reassure stakeholders.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next funding round
watchlist.body: With $190 million in hand, True Anomaly may be looking for strategic partnerships or additional funding to scale operations further.

watchlist.title: Defense budget discussions heat up
watchlist.body: As FY27 budget discussions progress, expect more insights into how much cash will flow into space resilience projects.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
